clue.text: Endless reading for a boss

indicators.note: endless asks for the word for reading to lose its final letter

parts.note: study is reading or learning, as in a study of the text

explanation.surface: Someone reads interminably to impress or serve their employer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' is not an employer but a raised knob or ornament on a surface, the sense that matches a stud.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a protruding knob, such as the metal decoration on a shield or belt, which is also called a stud.

clue.text: Worst type of underground heating?

parts.note: the underground place with the most dreadful heating is the infernal pit of damnation, whose flames burn sinners

explanation.surface: A grumble about a poor underfloor or geothermal heating system.
explanation.definitionFit: The flames of the underworld where sinners are punished are the fiercest, most dreaded heat below ground.

clue.text: End of spinnaker in large sailing ship

indicators.note: in places the picked letter inside the word for large

parts.note: big means large

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word spinnaker

explanation.surface: The tip of a spinnaker sail on a big sailing ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted, square-rigged vessel is a classic type of sailing ship.

clue.text: Painless exercise for dogs

indicators.note: exercise suggests putting the letters of painless through their paces into a new order

explanation.surface: Easy, gentle walks recommended for pet dogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Springers and cockers are breeds of gundog, examples of dogs.

clue.text: Ernest goes out for records

indicators.note: goes out suggests the name Ernest is disordered, broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Ernest leaves the house to buy some vinyl records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Records' looks like a noun for music discs but is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To record something in a ledger or log is to write it in, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Angry expressions that call for solutions

parts.note: cross means angry
words are expressions, things said

explanation.surface: Heated remarks that demand a fix to some quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Each grid puzzle of clues demands its answers be found, so it is something calling for solutions.

clue.text: It grows more by development

indicators.note: development suggests the letters of more by grow into a new shape

explanation.surface: Something that increases more and more through a process of development.
explanation.definitionFit: An unborn offspring in its early stage is a thing that keeps growing and developing.

clue.text: Drug found in a police department

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police forces

explanation.surface: Narcotics turn up inside a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for the hallucinogen LSD, a recreational drug.

clue.text: With time, successor of both

parts.note: an heir is one who succeeds to a title or estate

explanation.surface: Given time, someone will succeed to both titles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a possessive: something belonging to both people is theirs.
explanation.definitionFit: The possessive pronoun means belonging to them, so of the pair, i.e. of both.

clue.text: Father goes to Minorca, having break that's all-inclusive

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

indicators.note: having a break suggests Minorca is broken into pieces and reassembled

explanation.surface: Dad flies to the Spanish island of Minorca on an all-inclusive package holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A view or survey that takes in everything around is wide-ranging, effectively all-inclusive.

clue.text: Horse-drawn vehicle industry

definitions.meaning: a public stagecoach, especially in France

explanation.surface: The trade that builds carriages for horses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a French stagecoach and painstaking effort, here called industry.

clue.text: Scrap when Communist is told to be quiet!

parts.note: sh is the sound used to tell someone to be quiet
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A political argument ends when the Communist is silenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight, which suits the surface, but here it is a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a small torn piece, like a strip or fragment of paper.

clue.text: I meant a change to liven things up

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of the letters of I meant a

explanation.surface: Someone explains they intended a fresh change to brighten the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring life and energy to something is to enliven it, the verb's core sense.

clue.text: His professionalism may be brought into play

definitions.text: His professionalism may be brought into play

parts.words: His professionalism may be brought into play
parts.note: a performer's craft is used in a stage drama: a play is literally where his skill is put to work

explanation.surface: Someone's expertise could be called upon when needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brought into play' is the idiom for put to use, but read literally it puts someone into a theatrical play.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer's professional skill is exercised inside a theatre piece.

clue.text: Improve meal or I eat out

indicators.note: out suggests the letters of meal or I eat are put out of order

explanation.surface: Advice to get better by eating a meal, or dining out.
explanation.definitionFit: To ameliorate is a formal synonym for making something better.

clue.text: Short of shotguns?

parts.note: looks like lacking guns, but means the type of shotgun with shortened barrels

explanation.surface: An armoury running low on shotguns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' suggests not having enough, but it describes a shotgun whose barrels have been cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Shotguns with barrels cut short are known by this hyphenated term, favoured by robbers.

clue.text: Given the sack with enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: filled with zeal, as in excited or inspired

explanation.surface: Someone eagerly accepting being dismissed from their job.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both dismissed from work and stirred up with eagerness, as in fired up.

clue.text: No, no, not here!

definitions.note: the insistent refusal of one place points to the other place, over yonder

indicators.note: the second no means without, so the word not is written without the letters of the first No

parts.note: the letters N and O, removed from not

explanation.surface: Someone firmly redirecting a person who has picked the wrong spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' (meaning without) takes NO out of NOT, leaving T, and HERE follows. The whole clue is also the definition: not here but over yonder.
explanation.definitionFit: Insisting on the other place, away from this spot, points to a location over yonder.

clue.text: Due to take bus back

indicators.note: back means the word bus is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Someone about to catch the bus home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due' is a noun here: a sub is a subscription, a fee one owes.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscription paid to a club is a membership due, informally shortened.

clue.text: Subsidiary offices of the Forestry Commission?

definitions.text: Subsidiary offices of the Forestry Commission?

parts.words: Subsidiary offices of the Forestry Commission?
parts.note: local offices of a firm share their name with the limbs of trees, which a forestry body manages; the Forestry Commission is the UK body that runs public woodland

explanation.surface: Asking about the local outposts of Britain's state woodland agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Local offices of an organisation and the boughs of a tree share one word, apt for a forestry body.

clue.text: Appeal in two ways

definitions.note: to appeal to an authority for a decision is to submit a matter to it

indicators.note: in two ways says the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: to appeal to an authority for a decision is to submit a matter to it

explanation.surface: Making an appeal on two separate grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer to an authority is to have recourse to it, to appeal to it for a decision.

clue.text: Inferior sort of poker, perhaps?

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, to sort out the letters of inferior

explanation.surface: A rather second-rate kind of poker player or poker hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poker' suggests the card game, but it is the metal rod for stirring a fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireside poker is one example of a fire iron, alongside tongs and shovel.

clue.text: Pause as priest turns a key

indicators.note: turns suggests priest is turned around into a different order

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A cleric stops as he turns a key in a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: A respite is a short break or interval of relief, a pause.

clue.text: Score as a writer

definitions.meaning: to mark or scratch a line on wood or metal with a pointed tool
a copyist or clerk who writes out documents

explanation.surface: Someone who composes music working as an author.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for marking with a point and a noun for a copyist or author.

clue.text: Make attractive object — a listening device

parts.note: an end is an aim or object
the ear is the organ for hearing

explanation.surface: Designing a desirable gadget for eavesdropping.
explanation.definitionFit: To make someone loved or liked is to render them attractive to others.

clue.text: Fool's rude, that's for certain

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: a loose signal: rude is treated as something that is altered, its letters reshuffled

explanation.surface: Remarking that a fool is undoubtedly ill-mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak: 'that's' rearranges RUDE into URED; the blog likewise settles on 'that's for' for want of anything better.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sure or guaranteed is having something settled beyond doubt, certain.

clue.text: Panic, losing head, and slip

indicators.note: losing head asks for the first letter of the word for panic to go

parts.note: terror is extreme fear, panic

explanation.surface: Someone panics, loses their head and stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, synonym for a blunder.

clue.text: Dutch product manufactured to be sent North

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending the word North means reading it upwards, in reverse

parts.note: made means manufactured

explanation.surface: Goods made in the Netherlands and exported northwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A round cheese with red wax rind made in the Netherlands is a famous Dutch product.

clue.text: Design pet device, but not what it seems at first

definitions.text: not what it seems at first

indicators.note: design is read as a verb: rearrange the letters of pet device into a new design

explanation.surface: An invention for pets that turns out to be something other than it looked.
explanation.definitionFit: Something misleading gives a false impression, so it is not what it appears to be.

clue.text: Old northerner caught in a trap

indicators.note: in puts the abbreviation inside the word for a trap

parts.note: a pit is a hole dug as a trap
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An ancient tribesman snared in a trap.
explanation.definitionFit: The Picts were an ancient people of northern Scotland, so one is an old northerner.

clue.text: Mount found in Estonia, oddly enough

indicators.note: oddly picks the odd-numbered letters of the word Estonia

explanation.surface: A mountain turns up in Estonia, surprisingly.
explanation.walkthrough: Estonia is flat, which is what makes the surface's 'oddly enough' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is called Mount Etna.

clue.text: Judge a little speed to be about right

indicators.note: about puts the phrase for a little speed around the letter for right

parts.note: a bit means a little
rate means speed

explanation.surface: A judge warning a motorist who is going slightly too fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A little is A BIT, two words, and R sits just after its A.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to settle a dispute as an impartial referee, to sit in judgment.

clue.text: Symbol of sovereignty King Charles had to acknowledge

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
to own is to admit or acknowledge

explanation.surface: King Charles had to recognise the emblem of royal power.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal headgear worn by a monarch is the chief emblem of sovereign rule.
